A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the duration of the innate antiviral state is controlled by two distinct mechanisms: (1) RIG-I and (2) TNF α.

(i) RIG-I is required to initiate the antiviral transcription program, whereas MDA-5 sustains the response by inhibiting IRF-3 proteolysis; (ii) TNFα acts synergistically with IFNβ to trigger late antiviral genes, including the DUOX2-DUOXA2 genes, which are required to sustain IFN production.
“We identified two distinct mechanisms that contribute to control the duration of IFN-mediated antviral response in human airway cells infected with Paramyxoviridae.”
The main takeaway from our work is that
both RIG-I and its downstream effector MDA5 are required to sustain the antiviral state in the context of Paramyxovirus infection, but through two different mechanisms.
the innate antiviral immune response relies on a complex and dynamic network of signaling pathways.
the duration of the type I interferon response can be controlled by two distinct mechanisms, which involve RIG-I, MDA5, TNF α and DUOX2.
